name: Sidon
title: Canaan's firstborn son
summary: Sidon was the firstborn son of Canaan, grandson of Ham, and great-grandson of Noah. He is regarded as the patriarch of the Sidonians and the founder of the ancient Phoenician city of Sidon. In the Bible, he is mentioned primarily in genealogies as part of the list of nations after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Sidon mentioned in the Table of Nations
keyEvents.description: Sidon is listed as Canaan's firstborn son in the Table of Nations in Genesis, which describes the nations that descended from Noah's sons after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Canaan's lineage in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Sidon is again mentioned as Canaan's firstborn in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles, confirming his place in the history of the people.

keyEvents.title: The curse on Canaan and its significance
keyEvents.description: Noah's curse on Canaan, Sidon's father, following the incident with Ham, had consequences for all of Canaan's descendants, including the Sidonians.

keyEvents.title: Canaan's borders include Sidon
keyEvents.description: Canaan's territory is described with Sidon as the northern border, highlighting the city's prominent role among the Canaanite peoples.

keyEvents.title: The Sidonites as part of the promised land
keyEvents.description: The Sidonites, descendants of Sidon, were later mentioned among the peoples living in the promised land that the Israelites were to occupy.
